rules.mapping: routes over the versioned `CNA_KeyboardState` 256-slot bit field the C API already had. `cna_keyboard_state_init` reproduces the default constructor and `_init_from_keys` **both** canonical set-taking constructors, since an initializer list and an unordered set are the same deduplicated array in C. The indexer becomes `_get_key_state`, and equality, inequality, the hash and the string each get their own route. **Documented deviation:** the canonical constructors silently drop a key outside the 256-slot field; C refuses instead, so a caller can never lose a key without being told, and the refusal matches every other keyboard route
rules.tests: `InputSnapshotsSmoke.c` covers the empty default, a construction whose duplicate key contributes once, the out-of-range refusal, the indexer in both states, equal and unequal comparisons in both directions, hash agreement for equal snapshots, the exact fixed string with a too-small capacity writing nothing, and every null and invalid-snapshot refusal, under HEADLESS, SDL_RENDERER and SOFTWARE

rules.mapping: one `cna_keyboard_*` route per canonical static, each taking an active game handle for the same reason the gamepad queries do. The class itself has no handle: its canonical constructor is deleted and every member is static. The player-slot overload becomes `cna_keyboard_get_state_for_player`, which reports the same snapshot for every slot because CNA has one keyboard. The two name families use the project count/copy protocol and their reverse lookups take a borrowed `CNA_StringView`, so no `std::string` crosses the boundary; an unknown name answers with the canonical none identity rather than failing
rules.tests: `InputSnapshotsSmoke.c` asserts every slot reports the identical snapshot, the modifier mask stays inside the defined bits, the scancode translation stays in range, both name families round-trip through count/copy and back through the reverse lookup, an unknown name answers `CNA_KEY_NONE`, and every out-of-range-key, out-of-range-slot, invalid-view and null-output refusal, under HEADLESS, SDL_RENDERER and SOFTWARE

rules.mapping: `CNA_KeyModifiers` and the `CNA_KEY_MODIFIER_*` identities at the canonical bit values, plus `CNA_KEY_MODIFIER_ALL`. **Borrowed into CBIND-037B4a** from the input-extension slice, because `Keyboard::GetModStateEXT` returns it and cannot be mapped without it.
